name: libunwind

patches.replace:

patches.reason: Same as libcxxabi/recipe.json's matching patch: confirmed for real ("lld: error: unable to find library -lmingw32" and 15 siblings) building libc++abi; libunwind's own src/CMakeLists.txt has the identical line.

notes: extra_checkout_dirs (cmake/, runtimes/cmake/): libunwind/CMakeLists.txt is not self-contained -- it include()s shared LLVM CMake utility modules from these two sibling top-level directories (HandleCompilerRT.cmake and LLVMCheckCompilerLinkerFlag.cmake live in cmake/Modules/, HandleFlags.cmake lives in runtimes/cmake/Modules/), which a sparse-checkout of just libunwind/ alone does not carry. Confirmed for real: the first configure attempt without these failed with three separate "include could not find requested file" errors, one per missing module, only surfacing them one at a time as each earlier include() itself got past its own missing-file error. tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's fetch_recipe() copies these as siblings of libunwind/ under the shared source root, matching the relative ../cmake path libunwind/CMakeLists.txt itself expects.

macOS is deliberately excluded via target_os: Darwin's own libSystem provides a real system unwinder (compact unwind info, not the Itanium DWARF-CFI-based mechanism this project's other two hosts need), and the existing macOS crt-libcxx-smoke run already exercises real exception throw/catch successfully with no libunwind at all -- matches upstream LLVM's own default of LIBCXXABI_USE_LLVM_UNWINDER=OFF for Apple targets. Linux and Windows both build this from source rather than linking a host-installed libunwind package: a Linux distro's own libunwind-dev is easy to reach for, but linking it would put a DT_NEEDED on a library this project does not own or control the build of into every C++ binary this project ships (including its own libc++.so in the rootfs) -- a real runtime dependency, not a cosmetic shortcut, and one this project has consistently avoided elsewhere (../libcxx and ../libcxxabi are built from source rather than using host libstdc++/libc++ for the same reason; -lpthread/-lrt were absorbed into libc specifically so a host pthread/rt library could never leak into a Bionic-shaped binary; CRTGFX_ENABLE_SKIA's own policy states outright "never link host libc++ as a substitute"). This is a genuinely different case from CI's libc++-dev/libc++abi-dev install (see HISTORY.md's 2026-08-21 CI entry): that is a build-time-only requirement so Clang's own compiler-ABI-detection step can run while compiling *this project itself* -- it never ends up linked into anything this project ships.

Android removed the old platform/external/libunwind project in 2021; the current source policy is AOSP toolchain/llvm-project/libunwind (a full LLVM monorepo mirror -- fetched via a partial clone + cone sparse-checkout scoped to just the libunwind/ subpath, not the whole tree, confirmed to keep the fetch to tens of MB rather than the full monorepo).

libcxxabi's own recipe.json does depend on this one building first ("dependencies": ["libunwind"]) and does reference this recipe's own install output directly, via a windows-only CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS override pointing at @INSTALL_PREFIX@/lib/libunwind.dll.a -- an earlier version of this note claimed no LIBCXXABI-side reference was needed at all, which held for the *static* cxxabi_static/libc++abi.a build (confirmed: it links clean with zero libunwind anywhere in scope, since a static archive step never checks for undefined references) but turned out wrong for the *shared* cxxabi_shared/libc++abi.dll build, which -- unlike an ELF .so -- must resolve every referenced symbol (_Unwind_Resume, _Unwind_RaiseException, vtable for std::logic_error/std::bad_cast/..., etc.) at its own link time on Windows, confirmed for real via 'ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: _Unwind_Resume' and nine siblings. See ../libcxxabi/recipe.json's own notes for the fuller writeup; tools/crt-c++'s separate per-OS cxx_runtime_libs link (Windows: the sysroot-staged archive/import library this recipe also produces; Linux, once reached: a bare -lunwind against the host install) still exists for the *static*-linkage final-consumer case, which remains genuinely link-time-only as originally designed.

LIBUNWIND_HAS_PTHREAD_LIB=OFF on Windows: cmake/config-ix.cmake's own check_library_exists(pthread pthread_once ...) is a false positive under this build -- the same STATIC_LIBRARY-TryCompile-never-links root cause already diagnosed for LIBCXXABI_HAS_CXA_THREAD_ATEXIT_IMPL on Linux (see ../libcxxabi/recipe.json's notes): tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's common_cmake_args() sets CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE=STATIC_LIBRARY globally, so check_library_exists()'s own internal try_compile only ever builds a .obj referencing pthread_once and never actually attempts the link that would fail, so it reports the library 'found' unconditionally. Confirmed for real: unwind_shared_objects's link failed with 'lld: error: unable to find library -lpthread' -- correctly so, since this project deliberately has no separate pthread library at all (matching modern Bionic, -lpthread/-lrt are absorbed into libc; see AGENTS.md's build/runtime boundary principles). LIBUNWIND_HAS_DL_LIB is left alone: -ldl in that same failed link command did not error, because unlike pthread this project genuinely does ship a separate libdl the linker successfully resolves.

source.ref pinned 2026-08-21 (was refs/heads/main): captured via `git ls-remote https://android.googlesource.com/toolchain/llvm-project refs/heads/main`, which returned 37f38d1f3276b62fba09462ab4807dce846c732d that day. A floating branch ref means a rebuild months later can silently fetch different upstream source with no signal beyond a patch's own `find` text no longer matching (and only for the specific text a patch actually touches -- everything else could drift with zero signal at all) -- a real reproducibility gap this project already has explicit discipline against elsewhere (own the toolchain, no untracked floating dependencies). This also required a real fetch_recipe() fix, not just a JSON edit: `git clone --branch <sha>` does not work against this project's actual git host (confirmed for real: android.googlesource.com's Gerrit/JGit backend rejects it outright, "Remote branch <sha> not found in upstream origin"), only a plain `git fetch origin <ref>` does (confirmed to work identically for both a branch name and a raw commit SHA) -- see tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's own updated comment at the fetch step for the fuller story. Re-pin by re-running the same git ls-remote command and updating this value (and this note's own date) -- never by switching back to a floating ref.
